text:
taylor: FYI PR #9284 is ready for code review but I'm keeping it gated on the RFC/arch check. RFC: https://rwd.infer/rfcs/204-routing-fallbacks (short summary below).

- change: introduce policy-layer routing to prefer local quantized variants, fallback to hosted when capacity low
- impact: adds routing config + a small datastore index for model fallbacks

Can someone from architecture take a look? I want to avoid surprises during canary. cc @marco @kai

anya: thanks, pinging product questions now — what's the user-visible behavior during fallback?

kai: quick note — CI shows perf tests flaky on long sequences, can you paste the perf profile and the new config snippet?

devbot: CI • build #9284/test-123 · all checks passed · perf-suite queued

taylor: pasted config and perf note below:
```
routing_policy:
  primary: model-q4_0
  fallback: model-fp16-hosted
  max_latency_ms: 200
  safety: allow_partial_cache:true
```
perf summary: median latency up ~8% on 4k tokens in 1 client workload; 99p stays under SLO with canary batching tweaks. I added a short rollout plan in the PR description.

sam: quick question — does this change require DB migration? if yes we need ops window.

taylor: no schema migration. datastore index is ephemeral and created on startup; ops involvement minimal.

marco: I'll review the RFC + PR today. Two asks up front: (1) we need a clear fallback ordering matrix in the RFC (region, instance type, model family), (2) add a canary kill-switch in the console config (manual abort). Can you add both?

taylor: yep will update RFC and add a kill-switch toggle in the rollout document. ETA 3pm PT.

kai: also please add the perf test command you used and the raw numbers in the PR so SRE can reproduce.

taylor: added perf command and raw numbers to PR; linked the perf artifacts.

devbot: CI • perf-suite · run complete · artifacts: https://ci.internal/runs/9284/perf

marco: skimmed the RFC draft. The fallback ordering matrix looks fine after one tweak (prefer regional hosted before remote-hosted). That reduces cross-region egress risk. Made a small inline suggestion.

anya: product approves the user-visible behavior (graceful degrade -> user sees spinner then hosted result). documented in PR.

marco: OK I'm good with the design once the kill-switch is explicit in the console UI docs and there's a note about quota impacts. I left an approval comment on the PR.

kai: LGTM from infra side after CI artifacts attach the perf logs. left an approval.

taylor: thanks all — PR updated with kill-switch docs + perf logs. @marco can you confirm final arch stamp and I can merge during tomorrow's low-traffic window (8am PT)?

marco: stamped. please do canary for 2h at 1% then 10% then 100% with abort if 95p latency regresses >15%.

taylor: will do. scheduling merge for 2024-11-07 08:00 PT and will monitor. closing the loop here — thanks! :rocket:
